events.title: Output collapse: GDP per capita fell 15%
events.detail: Real GDP per capita fell from 1,160 to 987 (constant 2015 US$) in a single year.
events.source: derived: World Bank GDP per capita
events.contested: A one-year collapse of this size usually has several causes at once - war, currency crisis, commodity price, or the end of a political order. This marker says it happened; it does not say why.

events.title: Inflation crossed 50% (reached 56%)
events.detail: Consumer price inflation rose from 29.8% to 56.1%, crossing the 50% threshold.
events.source: derived: World Bank consumer price inflation
events.contested: The 50% line is a convention, not a natural boundary. Official inflation statistics are also among the most manipulated numbers governments publish, so the true figure may be higher than the one recorded here.

events.title: Economic Recovery Programme
events.detail: Ghana devalued the cedi sharply, liberalised prices and cut public employment under an IMF and World Bank supported programme.
events.contested: Often cited as structural adjustment's best African case, with sustained growth resuming. Sceptics note the low starting base after years of collapse and the scale of external financing that accompanied it.
